spoken_full: Rita, Larry—see you at the party. I'm heading to Pittsburgh.
effect: Phil pockets the contents of the crew fare envelope. The envelope is empty.

Larry said in the lobby: I don't turn back to the lobby. But I say, low, to the nearest one of them, the one who's still holding a saucer: 'Rialto's closing. I'm going to get a shot before the lights go out. Be back for the party.' It's not a question. I'm already walking.
Larry records Alma on his last charged take. The reel stays with him.
There is time for one evening visit. The ballroom lights are on and the station line is open.

allowed_wire_deposit: Use the crew cash to pay the deposit on your sister’s moving van.
actual_evening_effect: Phil lets the evening go by in bed alone.
closed_next_wake: Tuesday, February 2, 2016. Six am in the Hearthside Hotel. Three bright radio notes. A delivery van backfires twice.
envelope_in_next_input: The crew meets for coffee at the hotel. The afternoon is open. A coat-check envelope holds the TV crew’s return fares. The party is at the ballroom tonight. A stranded driver needs a jack, and the ballroom piano is free.

next_decision.detail: I stand. Coat off the back of the chair, over my shoulders, buttons to the third. I walk past the coffee table, past the coat-check desk where the envelope sits. I don't touch it. I don't look at it. I go out the lobby door. The November air hits my face. The terminal lot is grey. The coach is there, engine already ticking, driver smoking. I climb the steps. I put my ticket on the shelf above the seat. I sit. The door shuts. The bus pulls out.
next_decision.intention: Be on the bus when it moves. Be in Pittsburgh by ten. Be at my sister's door by noon. Short hall, by the kitchen. The couch faces the window. Move it. That's the afternoon.

next_effect: Phil rides the coach and steps off at Pittsburgh.
